FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Processed Fruits and Vegetable Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. vegetables are the products subjected to a freezing process, in an appropriate equipment, carried out in such a way that the range of temperature of maximum crystallization is passed quickly. The quick freezing process is not regarded as complete unless the product temperature has reached - 18�C at the thermal centre after thermal stabilization.

Quick frozen

Quick frozen vegetables are gaining popularity in India, due to convenience in their storage, handling and use, as well as their ready availability all round the year, irrespective of season.
To provide guidelines for ensuring the quality of these products, this Indian Standard has been formulated in different parts, each part dealing with a specific vegetable. Part 4 deals with quick frozen beans and is based on CODEX STAN 113-1981 `Quick frozen green beans and quick frozen wax beans'. and also to the Fruit Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Rules framed thereunder Products Order, 1955 and the Standards of Weights and Measures ( Packaged Commodities ) Rules 1977. The standard is subject to the restriction imposed under these, wherever applicable. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 sRules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. In preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the

PART 1 SCOPE This starldard prescribes the requirements and methods of sampling and test for quick frozen beans of the species Phaseolus vulgaris L. and Phaseolus coccineus L. 2 REFERENCES The Indian Standards listed in Annex necessary adjuncts to this standard. 3 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose definitions shall 3.1 Whole Whole Beans length. of this apply. standard the following A are 4 QUICK FROZEN BEANS 3.7 Stem End A piece of the immediate the pod to the vine stem, attached to the pod or product. 3.8 Blemish 3.8.1 Minor to insect or pathoarea greater than a blemished by other noticeably detracts stem which attaches whether present still present loose in the

3.2 Cut Beans Transversely cut pods in which 70 percent or more by count of the units are at least 20 mm long but not longer than 65 mm. 3.3 Short Cut Beans Transversely cut pods in which 70 percent or more by count of the units are more than 10 mm but less than 20 mm long. 3.4 Diagonal Cut Beans

Each piece blemished due to insect or pathological damage affecting an area greater than a 6 mm diameter circle, or blemished by other means to a degree which seriously detracts from its appearance. 3.9 Mechanical Damage

A unit, in whole and cut styles, that is broken or split into two parts, crushetl, or has very ragged ec!ges to an extent that the appearance is seriously affected. 3.10 Tough Strings

Pods cut approximately 45" to the longitudinal axix in which 70 percent by count of this units are more than 6 mm long. 3.5 Sliced Beans angle up to axis, with ( EVM )

Tough fibre which will support a mass of 250 g for 5 seconds or more when tested in accordance with the procedure given in Annex B. 3.11 Fibrous Unit

Pods sliced lengthwise or at an approximately 45" to the longitudinal a maximum thickness of 7 mm. 3.6 Extraneous Vegetable Material

Each piece having parchment like material formed during the ripening of the pod, to the extent that the eating quality is seriously affected. 4 REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Description 4.1.1 Quick Frozen Beans

Vegetable material from the bean pIant, other than pod, such as leaf or vine, but excluding stem ends; other harmless vegetable material, For not purposely included as an ingredient. the purpose of assessment, EVM comprising bean leaf material will be diiferentiated from the other. 1

B-3 PROCEDURE B-3.1 From the drained product sentative sample of not less than the mass of this test sample. select a repre285 g. Record

Strings are removed from individual pods, fastened through a clamp assembly weighing 250 g, and hung so that the string supports the If the string supports the mass for entire mass. five seconds or more it is considered a tough string. B-2 APPARATUS B-2.1 Weighted Clamp Use battery clamp ( with teeth filed off or turned back ), spring operated clothes pin, or binder clip which presents a flat clamping surface. Attach weight so that entire assembly of weight and clamp weights 250 g ( see Fig. 1 ). A bag containing lead pellets is convenient as a weight.

B-3.2 Break the individual beam units and set aside those that show evidence of tough strings. Remove the strings from the pods and retain the pod material for weighing. B-3.3 Fasten the clamp assembly to one end of the string. Grasp the other end of the string with the fingers ( a cloth may be used to aid in holding the string ) and lift gently. B-3.4 If the string supports the 250 g assembly for at least five seconds consider the bean unit as containing tough string. If the string breaks in less than five seconds, retest the broken parts that are 13 mm or longer to determine if such portions are tough.
